items.t: Stalls or loses power while driving
items.note: Prices the most common named cause. A shop should read the codes first: misfires or traction control faults need different repairs. YourMechanic: about $387 average total; its per-year quotes run about $680–$700.

items.t: Timing chain stretch, rattle and check engine light
items.job: Replace timing chain, chain guides and crank sprocket
items.note: Parts from KBB's 2015 Juke dealer parts figure ($348–$392). KBB lists only $528–$584 labor, which looks low because the front timing cover must come off; hours are inferred from YourMechanic's Juke timing cover replacement (about $1,064 average labor; per-year quotes about $1,860–$2,090 total). Owner-reported costs: $900–$1,200 quoted if caught before the chain breaks, about $2,000–$2,100 at repair (NHTSA complaints); a broken chain can mean a $5,000–$9,000 engine.

items.t: Turbo air inlet tube can separate and stall engine (recall)
items.job: Free recall repair at a Nissan dealer
items.note: Recall flat rate: 0.2 h to inspect, 0.3 h to inspect and replace the tube.

items.t: Check engine light for evaporative (EVAP) leak
items.note: Based on YourMechanic, since no parts-retailer page was reached: average $294 total ($199 parts, $95 labor); per-year quotes about $490–$520 total, so the parts high end is inferred from those quotes minus labor. A loose gas cap or O-ring may cost far less, so test first.

items.t: Clicking from axles when pulling away
items.note: Based on YourMechanic, since no parts-retailer page was reached: average $425 ($145 parts, $280 labor); per-year quotes $582–$833 by axle position, dealers up to about $1,380. Parts high end inferred from those quotes minus labor. The bulletin fix (cleaning and greasing the axle-to-hub joint) usually costs much less.

items.t: Door won't lock or unlock from outside handle button
items.note: Based on YourMechanic, since no parts-retailer page was reached: average $219 ($79 parts, $140 labor); per-year quotes $304–$444 total, dealers up to about $750. Parts high end inferred from those quotes minus labor.

items.t: Worn tie rod ends cause clunk or loose steering
items.job: Replace one tie rod end (alignment extra)
items.note: A mechanic on YourMechanic puts each tie rod end at about $50 from a parts store. YourMechanic: average $162 total ($67 parts, $95 labor); front per-year quotes $266–$324, so the parts high end is inferred from those minus labor. Rear tie rods are quoted higher ($716–$721). A wheel alignment afterward is extra.

items.t: Won't start from a drained battery
items.note: YourMechanic Juke battery replacement: $291 average ($151 parts, $140 labor); hours are that labor charge at the site's $120-160/hr rate, since no book time is published. YourMechanic per-year estimates run $447-$459 and shop/dealer quotes $524-$775. Estimator used as the basis because no parts-plus-labor source was found. If a parasitic draw keeps killing new batteries, finding the faulty circuit (often the key switch circuit or power distribution module) costs extra.

items.t: Fuel pump or fuel level sender fails
items.job: Replace the in-tank fuel pump module (includes the level sender)
items.note: Parts: YourMechanic average parts $455 (low); genuine Nissan in-tank pump 17040-1KM1A lists at $784.07 MSRP ($513.72 discounted). Hours are YourMechanic's $203 average labor charge at the site's $120-160/hr rate, since no book time is published. A failed high-pressure engine pump (16630-1KC0C, $750 MSRP) is a separate, pricier job, and a bad relay is much cheaper, so have fuel pressure tested first. RepairPal fuel level sending unit replacement: $1,078-$1,276 total.
